textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of ONE human contractile CARDIOMYOCYTE (working heart muscle cell), centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around the structures so labels can be attached later. The illustration's own neutral dark charcoal background must extend and touch all four edges of the canvas, filling it completely corner to corner. Do NOT draw any border line, rectangle outline, frame, mat, margin band, vignette or letterbox bar around the artwork, and do NOT draw the picture as a sheet or card lying on a surface — there must be no visible seam between an inner picture and an outer margin.

HOUSE LOOK — match a refined educational plate exactly: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette of soft dusty tints (never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (never heavy black cartoon strokes), gentle soft shading with subtle dimensionality, and each structure its own distinct soft colour fill.

MORPHOLOGY: the cell is a short, stocky, roughly cylindrical striated muscle cell lying diagonally across the frame, only about five times longer than it is wide, and it BRANCHES into a Y at each end — this branching is essential and must be unmistakable. At the tip of every branch the cell butts END-TO-END against a neighbouring cardiomyocyte (the neighbours are drawn faintly and cropped by the frame edge, clearly subordinate to the central cell). Each of those end-to-end contacts is a dark, STEP-LIKE, staircase-shaped transverse line running right across the full width of the fibre — the INTERCALATED DISC. Draw at least three of them, one per branch tip, always transverse to the fibre axis and never running lengthwise along the cell's flank.

INTERIOR (revealed by a neat long cutaway along the upper half of the cell):
- Parallel MYOFIBRILS running the length of the cell, each banded with regular, precisely aligned cross-striations: a darker dusty-rose A band alternating with a paler cream I band, and a crisp slate-blue Z-DISC line in the middle of every I band. The striations of neighbouring myofibrils line up in register across the whole cell.
- ONE single oval nucleus, muted blue-violet, sitting in the MIDDLE of the cell in a spindle-shaped myofibril-free clearing.
- Abundant amber-ochre MITOCHONDRIA with visible inner cristae, packed in dense longitudinal rows in every gap between the myofibrils and clustered around the nucleus — they should visibly occupy about a third of the interior, not a token few.
- Pale blue T-TUBULES: wide tubular invaginations of the surface membrane running straight into the cell interior, each one entering exactly at the level of a Z-disc, one per sarcomere.
- A pale lilac SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM meshwork sleeving the myofibrils, with a swollen terminal cisterna abutting each T-tubule.
- A thin teal-blue SARCOLEMMA outlining the whole cell.
- In an enlarged inset-free close-up region of one intercalated disc, show its three components distinctly: a broad sage-olive FASCIA ADHERENS band on the transverse step segments with actin filaments inserting into it, small warm-ochre DESMOSOME plaques also on the transverse segments, and bright teal GAP JUNCTION channel plaques on the longitudinal (lengthwise) segments of the same staircase.

DO NOT draw: a long unbranched multinucleated skeletal muscle fibre; a peripheral row of many nuclei flattened against the membrane; a smooth, tapered, unstriated smooth-muscle spindle; neuron-like dendrites, axons, growth cones, synapses or myelin; a neuromuscular junction or motor end plate; a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, flagella or cilia; T-tubules at the A-I junction. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars or watermarks anywhere in the image.
sem:
Photorealistic false-colour SCANNING ELECTRON MICROGRAPH of ONE isolated human contractile CARDIOMYOCYTE (working heart muscle cell), centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous empty margin. Fill the whole square edge to edge with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox bar, and do not render the image as a plate lying on a surface.

The specimen is a short, stocky, roughly cylindrical striated muscle cell resting on a subtly textured flat substrate, lying diagonally across the frame, only about five times longer than it is wide. It BRANCHES into a Y at each end — the branching must be unmistakable. At the tip of each branch the cell meets a neighbouring cardiomyocyte end to end, and each of those contacts shows as a pronounced, STEP-LIKE, staircase-shaped transverse ridge and groove running right across the full width of the fibre — the INTERCALATED DISC — with an interlocking, finger-like corrugated relief along the step faces. The neighbouring cells are cropped by the frame edge and clearly subordinate to the central specimen.

Render true 3D surface relief and nothing else: SEM shows only the outside, so draw NO internal organelles, NO nuclei, NO visible sarcomeres inside the cell. What the surface does reveal is a gentle regular transverse rippling of the sarcolemma over the underlying sarcomeres, a faint scalloped costamere pattern, and small round mouth openings of the T-tubules dimpling the surface in regular rows. Crisp fine surface texture, shallow depth of field so the far end falls softly out of focus, cool studio microscopy lighting with a gentle rim light.

False-colour palette: a warm dusty rose to soft salmon cell surface, the intercalated-disc step ridges picked out in a cooler teal-grey, on a neutral pale grey substrate and a dark uncluttered charcoal background.

DO NOT render: a long unbranched multinucleated skeletal muscle fibre; a smooth tapered unstriated smooth-muscle spindle; neuron-like dendrites, axons or synapses; a bacterium, cell wall, flagellum or cilium; duplicated specimens; any floating debris. Single specimen only, clearly dominant in the frame. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, instrument data bars or watermarks anywhere in the image.
watercolor:
Hand-painted WATERCOLOUR naturalist scientific plate of ONE human contractile CARDIOMYOCYTE (working heart muscle cell), in the composition of a 19th-century scientific atlas but anatomically modern and correct. Square 1:1, 1080x1080.

PAPER RULE (most important): the warm, softly mottled AGED PAPER is the background and it must FILL THE ENTIRE FRAME, edge to edge and corner to corner, with its grain and foxing running right off all four sides. Do NOT paint the artwork as a separate sheet, card or page lying on a table, desk or any surface. NO mat, NO border, NO frame, NO drop shadow, NO torn or deckled paper edge, NO grey or dark panel around a sheet, NO vignette, NO letterbox bars. There must be no visible edge of paper anywhere in the picture.

SUBJECT: the cell is large and centred, painted in rich translucent washes with fine ink linework for the outlines, and a soft darker wash halo laid directly on the paper behind it. It is a short, stocky, roughly cylindrical striated muscle cell lying diagonally, only about five times longer than it is wide, and it BRANCHES into a Y at each end — the branching must be unmistakable. At each branch tip it butts END TO END against a neighbouring cardiomyocyte, painted in paler washes and cropped by the frame edge; every one of those contacts is a dark, STEP-LIKE, staircase-shaped transverse ink line drawn right across the full width of the fibre — the INTERCALATED DISC. Draw at least three, always transverse to the fibre axis, never running lengthwise along a flank.

A painted cutaway along the upper half shows the interior: parallel MYOFIBRILS with regular fine cross-striations (deeper rose A bands, pale cream I bands, a fine ink Z-disc line down the centre of each I band, aligned in register); ONE oval violet-washed nucleus sitting in the MIDDLE of the cell in a myofibril-free clearing; abundant warm ochre MITOCHONDRIA with hinted cristae packed in long rows in every gap between the myofibrils, occupying about a third of the interior; wide pale-blue T-TUBULES dipping in from the surface exactly at the level of a Z-disc; a soft lilac SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM mesh sleeving the myofibrils; and, at the nearest intercalated disc, small teal gap-junction plaques on the lengthwise step faces and ochre desmosome dots with a sage fascia-adherens band on the transverse step faces.

Muted botanical-plate palette: dusty rose, cream, ochre, sage, soft slate blue, on warm cream paper.

DO NOT paint: a long unbranched multinucleated skeletal muscle fibre; a peripheral row of nuclei against the membrane; a smooth tapered unstriated smooth-muscle spindle; neuron-like dendrites, axons, synapses or myelin; a motor end plate; a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, flagella or cilia. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, handwriting, labels, arrows, scale bars, signatures or watermarks anywhere in the image.
